column2: FAO/ NASA Harvest Malawi Crop Cut Yield 2023
UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) & NASA Harvest, (2023). FAO/ NASA Harvest Malawi Crop Cut Yield 2023. (NASA Harvest Data Portal; V1) [data set].

The 2023 FAO/ NASA Harvest Malawi Crop Cut dataset provides sample crop cut yield data from selected maize fields across Kasungu District, Malawi that represent in season yield variability at the district level.
UN FAO, NASA Harvest, FAO Malawi, Ministry of Agriculture Malawi

The field location and field boundary and area in hectares was collected from every identified field. From each field a 10x10 meter crop cut was taken containing a nested 5x5 meter crop cut sub plot at the southwest corner of the 10x10 meter crop cut (See Figure 1). The location of the sample crop cuts was randomly selected using the length and width measurements of the field and ensuring that the randomly generated coordinates placed the sample crop cuts within the field boundaries and that no portion of the crop cut was within 5 meters of the field edge. At the randomly generated coordinate the 5x5 meter crop cut plot and 10x10 meter crop cut plots were 1. measured out, 2. demarcated, 3. harvested in sequence. The 5x5 meter sub plot was harvested first to ensure that no portion of the 5x5 was measured with the 10x10 plot. The maize cobs harvested from the sample crop cut plots were 1. cleaned, 2. Weighed, 3. counted 4. 20 percent of the cobs were randomly selected and dekerneled to assess the kernel weight and 5. measure the moisture content of the maize kernels to calculate dry weight of the kernels. The measurements were recorded using the Survey 123 application and a farmer survey was taken at each sampled field to record qualitative information related to yield including the farmer field practices and crop condition assessment.

The objective of the sampling frame was to select 100 villages from across Kasungu district, Malawi that represented in season yield variability at the district level. Villages were selected based on proximity to cropland by using a 2-kilometer buffer around each village and sampling the NASA Harvest 2020/2021 Malawi Cropland Mask to identify the villages with at least 75% cropland in the surrounding area, to define ‘rural villages’. From these identified villages NDVI values were calculated at the 95th percentile during the peak vegetative calendar. Within the 2-kilometer buffered villages, the average 95th percentile NDVI was used to classify each village into High, Medium and Low classifications using Natural Breaks (Jenks), relating to High, Medium and Low crop yields/ conditions based on the assumption high NDVI values correlate with higher yields. 100 villages were then randomly selected proportionally from these classifications to represent yield variability at the District level. This final sample was then provided to local partners to identify the final list of 90 villages where sample crop cuts would be taken from selected fields. To identify the selected fields within each selected village, a village representative was tasked with selecting representative fields that met the following criteria: primary crop is maize, field size is larger than .5 hectares, maize crop is at full maturity and no portion of the field has been harvested, selected fields are representative of crop condition variability at the village level. This was a necessary concession to ensure adequate participation in the crop cut exercise. The sampling frame protocol applied under this campaign is one that we expect to evolve in future campaigns to further test the best sampling methods for selecting field locations to represent yield variability in support of validation of training data.
